_comment: Critical-mutant manifest for tools/mutants.py (issue #18/#19, 'curl-style' assurance). Each entry BREAKS one security/correctness invariant by a precise reversible source transform; the named killer hosted test, after PASSING clean on pristine source (the baseline preflight), MUST then fail under the mutation (the mutant is KILLED). A SURVIVED mutant = the clean-passing test does not actually prove its invariant (a test defect). A BLOCKED mutant = an untrustworthy verdict: the killer did not pass on pristine source, the `find` pattern does not match exactly once (source drift), the mutated source failed to build (a compile failure is NEVER a kill), a timeout on a non-liveness mutant, or any infrastructure failure. Production code carries NO mutation macros; mutants live entirely here + in tools/mutants.py and every build/run happens in a private disposable snapshot, so the kernel source and the caller's worktree stay untouched. Keep the ENABLED set small and canonical (regression anchors whose killer test exists AND passes clean today). The DISABLED entries at the end are test-GAP markers: critical invariants whose killer test does NOT exist yet; they are enabled:false so `make mutants` stays green while documenting the missing coverage; enable each one when its killer test lands (and remove the placeholder find-string). Writing a deleter mutant as `if (0 && (<cond>))` keeps a variable used so -Werror does not turn a test gap into a spurious build failure. See docs/audit/2026-11-code-audit.md and docs/audit/2026-11-fix-gate.md (F01/F04) for provenance; AI-assisted, not human qualification.

mutants.invariant: je_pages_free rejects an out-of-window physical address BEFORE deriving a page index (prevents an OOB state[] write)
je_pages_init_pred is default-DENY: a page the predicate does not approve is RESERVED (the PR-H .bss-zero=ALLOW defect class)
mutants.killer: test_physmem: init state[] vs independent byte-level reference; exhaustion excludes reserved frames

mutants.invariant: resolve_slot denies a lookup whose handle lacks the required rights (a handle never grants more than it holds)
mutants.killer: test_handle: lookup with insufficient rights is DENIED

mutants.invariant: je_handle_duplicate can only REMOVE rights: a dup requesting rights not held by the source is DENIED (no privilege escalation by duplication)
mutants.killer: test_handle: duplicate requesting a superset of rights is DENIED

mutants.invariant: je_vm_image_validate rejects a descriptor whose segments overlap (or collide with the stack/guard) at page granularity
mutants.find: if (used[p]) return JE_ERR_INVALID; /* overlap or stack/guard */
mutants.replace: if (0 && (used[p])) return JE_ERR_INVALID; /* overlap or stack/guard */

mutants.invariant: je_fdt_parse rejects a blob whose magic is not JE_FDT_MAGIC (an untrusted non-DTB blob is never parsed as a DTB)
je_vm_audit rejects a page table where two arena offsets map the same physical frame (no user-visible aliasing of a single frame)
mutants.killer: GAP: no hosted negative test pokes a one-to-one violation into vm_fake (peer audit: SURVIVES). Add a poke-based negative test, then enable.

mutants.invariant: wait_register pins the endpoint record with an inflight ref so a parked waiter's record cannot be freed while it sleeps (no use-after-free in the timeout sweep)
mutants.killer: GAP: peer audit's probe dropped the inflight ref and the mutant SURVIVED (close both handles while a thread is parked -> record freed under the sleeper). Add the killer test, pin the exact find-string, then enable.

mutants.invariant: je_device_apply_dispatch grants ring-3 port I/O only to the device's owner (identity, not merely active)
mutants.killer: GAP: je_device_apply_dispatch has no hosted test (peer audit: DISPATCH-ANY-USER SURVIVES). Add owner / non-owner / post-revoke / closed-handle cases, pin the find-string, then enable.

mutants.invariant: the AArch64 page-table audit validates EVERY child table address (root membership + alignment) BEFORE dereferencing it, including in audit_alias_scan — a foreign/unvalidated sibling pointer is rejected, not followed
mutants.killer: GAP: CORRECTED per fix-gate F04. The earlier 'infinite recursion on a cycle' claim is WRONG — both walkers bound at level<3 and a root self-cycle already returns JE_ERR_INVALID. The REAL confirmed defect: audit_alias_scan (paging.c:456, reached via the recursive call at 466 from audit_table at 544) dereferences a child table address WITHOUT the root-membership check audit_table applies, so an otherwise-valid earlier leaf triggers an alias scan into an unvalidated later sibling (e.g. root[511]=0x30000000|3) -> ASan SEGV. Fix: a complete bounded structural pass that validates every table pointer before any alias/permission dereference; the foreign-sibling fixture must return INVALID, not crash. Add the hosted negative test, pin the find-string, then enable. OWNER-GATED (ARM paging, tested path).
